claim_details.claim: Cardiac biomarkers are substances released into the blood when the heart is damaged or under stress they are used to diagnose and manage heart conditions such as heart attacks and heart failure

The most commonly used cardiac biomarker is troponin — a protein that enters the bloodstream shortly after a heart attack and stays elevated for up to 2 weeks — and healthcare providers typically use a troponin test as the primary marker for heart damage from a heart attack or acute coronary syndrome (ACS)

Other cardiac biomarkers include creatinine kinase (CK) and its MB fraction, myoglobin, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), though some of these are less specific to the heart and can be elevated by skeletal muscle injury or other conditions

Additionally, natriuretic peptides such as B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal proBNP (NT-proBNP) are used to assess the strain on the heart in conditions like heart failure traditional markers like C-reactive protein (CRP) and uric acid are also used in some cases
